channel.title: In Context
channel.description: Essays on agentic AI, safety, and the practice of building with LLMs — by Aravind Singirikonda.

item.title: Engine, Track, Driver, Payload — a frame for enterprise GenAI
item.description: A simple mental model for getting enterprise GenAI past the demo stage and into the operating model — without breaking what makes the business work.

item.title: How to break into GenAI
item.description: I get asked this every week. The question has two distinct problems hidden inside it — learning the work and finding the job — and they have to be solved in parallel. Here's the version I keep sending people.

item.title: Articulate isn't wise
item.description: AI is now more articulate about grief, anxiety, and loneliness than most humans are about their own feelings. We trust the voice that sounds like it knows. That's quietly become the wrong move.

item.title: Education in the age of AI
item.description: Most schools optimize for recall, not understanding. The constraint that forced that trade-off just broke — and the version of education that's coming can be radically better, if we choose it.

item.title: The GenAI strategy stack — a framework for enterprise AI adoption
item.description: Every week I sit with companies working through their GenAI strategy. The same four-layer shape keeps showing up underneath every conversation — and the teams that ship invest across all of it.

item.title: The five-line Claude Code hook that gives me back 30 minutes a day
item.description: Kick off a Claude Code task, switch screens, get pulled into something else, come back 20 minutes later and find it sitting there waiting for a Yes/No. There's a dead-simple fix.

item.title: ccview — a tiny TUI companion for Claude Code
item.description: I've been running Claude Code for almost everything lately — personal finances, research, side projects. The output is great. The terminal is a terrible place to read it. So I built a small thing.

item.title: What "safe" means when you ship GenAI to an enterprise
item.description: When safety comes up in a customer conversation, it almost never means what the AI labs mean. Here's what enterprise safety actually involves — and where the two conversations finally meet.

item.title: The Flappy Bird test
item.description: When I want to know if a new coding assistant is actually any good, I ask it to build Flappy Bird. One small prompt catches almost everything that matters.
